prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: cancelling cover to save money. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 2)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member wants to cancel cover to save money, check whether the policy is still needed for an active mortgage or car finance requirement should confirm they understand the gap before I proceed."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member is under financial pressure, I look for cheaper options such as adjusting voluntary excess, arrangement."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the member is deciding under stress, I prefer to slow the conversation down and summarise the trade-off in plain language so they can make a proper informed choice."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the policy has limited time left to run, I check whether non-renewal is a better fit than immediate cancellation, because the timing can
